docRequirement: scheduled-tasks.md:130 binds a self-paced `/loop` to a model-callable `ScheduleWakeup` tool: "Claude calls the [`ScheduleWakeup` tool](/docs/en/tools-reference) with `stop: true`, which cancels the pending wakeup immediately", and "If an iteration ends without either rescheduling or stopping, Claude Code schedules one fallback wakeup about 20 minutes later and ends the loop when that iteration doesn't reschedule either." tools-reference.md:46 fixes the rest of the contract: ScheduleWakeup "Reschedules the next iteration of a [self-paced `/loop`] … Claude calls this at the end of each iteration to pick when the next one runs, between one minute and one hour out; you don't call it directly", `stop` is a named field, and "The pending wakeup appears in `session_crons` in [Stop hook input]". scheduled-tasks.md:74 adds that a dynamically scheduled loop "appears in your [scheduled task list] like any other task" and is subject to the seven-day expiry, but "The [jitter rules](#jitter) don't apply to it". Field spellings the page fixes: the tool name `ScheduleWakeup`, the field `stop`, the Stop-hook key `session_crons`. The delay field's name is NOT spelled anywhere on either page.

divergence: The whole self-paced half of the page is absent, not mis-keyed. There is no `ScheduleWakeup` tool (no schema, no registry entry, no handler, no port method), no dynamic `/loop` iteration for it to re-arm or stop, no ~20-minute fallback wakeup, and no representation of a wakeup that is a delay rather than a cron expression — `SessionCronRecord` can only express a cron string, so even a correctly-named tool would have nothing to write. Two sub-deltas are narrower and independently real: (1) `cronJitterOffsetMs` would apply jitter to a dynamic loop, contradicting scheduled-tasks.md:74, because `SessionCronRecord` has no no-jitter field; (2) `session_crons` in Stop hook input is already correct by construction — anything stored as a record projects — so tools-reference.md:46's Stop-hook clause needs no work once the wakeup IS a record. The fixed-interval half of the page (5-field dialect, 8-char ids, 50 cap, seven-day expiry, ID-derived jitter, once-a-second tick, symlink refusal, `NESSY_DISABLE_CRON`/`CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_CRON`) is at parity and is not part of this divergence.

change.what: Add two optional fields to `SessionCronRecord` (:54-65): `dynamic?: boolean` (this record is a self-paced loop — its fire time comes from a wakeup, not from `schedule`, and scheduled-tasks.md:74 exempts it from jitter) and `nextFireAt?: number` (epoch ms of the pending wakeup). Relax `isRecord` (:153-165) so a record carrying them still validates and one lacking them still loads — both must stay optional or every existing on-disk store is discarded. Thread both through `create` (:224-245) and add a `rearm(id, nextFireAt)` method to the `SessionCronStore` interface (:187-204) that rewrites `nextFireAt` the way `markFired` (:255-259) rewrites `lastFiredAt`. This is a persistence-boundary change: the file written by `writeState` (:181-185) keeps `schemaVersion: 1`, so the added fields must be forward- and backward-tolerant.

`cronJitterOffsetMs` (:72-94): return 0 immediately when `record.dynamic` — scheduled-tasks.md:74, "The jitter rules don't apply to it". `nextCronFireTime` (:100-114): when `record.dynamic`, return `record.nextFireAt` as a Date (or null when absent, which is what ends the loop) instead of parsing `record.schedule`. `planCronRestore` (:226-243) needs no branch — a dynamic record is `recurring`, so the existing seven-day bound already applies, which is what :74 requires; add the test that pins it rather than code.

Add `startSelfPaced({prompt})` (creates a `dynamic: true` record with the first `nextFireAt`), `rearm(id, delayMs)` (clamp to the documented one-minute-to-one-hour window from tools-reference.md:46, write `nextFireAt = now + delayMs`) and `stopWakeup(id)` (delete the record — `stop: true` "cancels the pending wakeup immediately", scheduled-tasks.md:130; reuse `remove` at :94-98, which already drops an enqueued fire). Add the fallback: when a dynamic record's fire is delivered by `flush` (:174-184) and the iteration ends without a `rearm` or `stopWakeup`, arm one wakeup ~20 minutes out and mark the record so the NEXT unrescheduled iteration deletes it — scheduled-tasks.md:130's two-step end. `flush` currently calls `markFired` for non-final fires; a dynamic record needs its `nextFireAt` cleared at the same point or it re-fires every tick.

Add `ScheduleWakeupSchema` next to the cron schemas (:246-260): the page names only `stop` (boolean), so spell that exactly; the delay field is undocumented and must be chosen and the choice recorded in the comment (the cron schemas' comment block at :236-244 is the precedent). Register `{ name: 'ScheduleWakeup', description: TOOL_DESCRIPTIONS.ScheduleWakeup, inputSchema: ScheduleWakeupSchema, executionMode: 'registry', safeMode: 'block', visibility: 'pi-only', handler: handleScheduleWakeup }` alongside :1082-1084 — `block` matches `CronCreate`/`CronDelete`, whose comment at :1073-1077 explains why a documented "Permission required: No" tool that writes a file is still not `allow`. Add `'ScheduleWakeup'` to `CRON_TOOL_NAMES` (:1172-1176) so `NESSY_DISABLE_CRON` removes it too — scheduled-tasks.md:208 disables the cron tools AND `/loop` together, and `getSessionToolDefs` (:1214-1226) reads that set.

New handler in the same file as the three cron handlers, following their exact shape (`safeParse` → `invalid`, `port(ctx, 'ScheduleWakeup')` → `isToolResult`, try/`failed`). `stop: true` calls the port's cancel path and reports the loop ended; otherwise it re-arms and reports the chosen delay. `isToolResult` (:32-34) narrows on `'create' in value`, so it keeps working when the port grows methods.

Extend the `cronPort` shape (:437-446) with `rearmWakeup(input: { delayMs: number }): Promise<{ firesAt: number }>` and `stopWakeup(): Promise<boolean>`. Optional members on the existing port rather than a new port, so a backend without a self-paced loop keeps failing the `ScheduleWakeup` call through the existing "unavailable for this backend" path at cron-tools.ts:26-30.

Extend the `cronPort` literal (:12130-12141) with the two new methods delegating to `SessionCronService`. `getOrCreatePiCronService` (:2735-2766) needs no change — the service is per session and already restored on resume. `buildHookTaskRegistryPort` (:5660-5666) needs no change either: it reads the store, so a dynamic loop stored as a record satisfies tools-reference.md:46's `session_crons` clause for free.

blastRadius: Two boundaries this repo treats as risk triggers. (1) PERSISTENCE: `SessionCronRecord` is written to disk by `writeState` (packages/shared/src/sessions/cron-store.ts:181-185) under the per-session cron file at `schemaVersion: 1`; adding fields means an older build reading a newer file must still validate it through `isRecord` (:153-165), which today drops any record failing its six required-field check. Covered by `packages/shared/src/sessions/cron-store.test.ts`. (2) WIRE: `SessionCronEntryV1` (packages/shared/src/automations/hook-task-registry.ts:64-71) is the Stop-hook payload's `session_crons` shape, re-exported from `packages/shared/src/automations/index.ts:69` and consumed in the payload type at `packages/shared/src/automations/types.ts:901`; adding a field there changes what every user hook script sees. Pinned by `packages/shared/src/agent/__tests__/pi-agent-lifecycle-hooks.test.ts:341-396` (present-empty arrays, and `recurring` per entry) and `packages/server-core/src/sessions/hook-task-registry-projection.test.ts:131-177`. Other readers: `SessionCronService` has 5 callers, all in `packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts`, with tests in `packages/server-core/src/sessions/session-cron-service.test.ts`; `SessionCronStore` has 5 callers across session-cron-service.ts and cron-store.ts; the tool-registry edit is read by `getSessionToolDefs` and therefore by all three projections (Claude, Pi, session-mcp-server) — the new tool must stay `visibility: 'pi-only'` or it surfaces on backends with no `cronPort`. `cronJitterOffsetMs` is called only from `nextCronFireTime`, so the jitter exemption is contained. Nothing here touches imported-plugin paths.
userImpact: None observable today. A user cannot reach the missing mechanism at all: there is no `/loop` command to type (no bundled command or skill exists — `apps/electron/resources/skills/` holds only `plugin-creator` and `skill-creator`), so no self-paced iteration can start and no wakeup can be pending. What a user CAN do is ask in chat for a repeating check, which the model serves with `CronCreate` on a fixed cron schedule; the visible difference from Claude Code is that the interval never adapts — a poll set to 5m keeps polling every 5 minutes after the build goes quiet, and the model has no way to end its own loop other than `CronDelete`, which it must choose to call. It would surface the moment a `/loop` host ships: a self-paced loop would then either never re-arm (loop dies after one iteration) or, if built on `CronCreate` alone, run on a jittered fixed schedule that scheduled-tasks.md:74 says must not be jittered.
